user_request: Build an AI document intelligence platform using AWS. It should allow users to upload PDF documents, extract text using OCR, store documents securely, provide semantic search and question answering using RAG, support user authentication, and expose APIs for integration with other enterprise systems. Prefer reusable open-source solutions where appropriate, but ensure the selected components have suitable licenses and acceptable security/maturity.
normalized_request: Build a cloud-native document intelligence platform on AWS that ingests PDFs, extracts text via OCR, stores documents securely, enables semantic search and RAG-powered question answering, enforces user authentication, and provides REST APIs for enterprise integration—leveraging open-source components where licensing and security posture are acceptable.

execution_plan.objective: Break down the AI document intelligence platform into discrete technical components: PDF upload/handling, OCR text extraction, secure document storage, semantic search indexing, RAG-based QA, user authentication, and REST API layer, identifying dependencies and data flows between them.

Identify open-source and public ecosystem candidates for each component (OCR engines, vector databases, embedding models, authentication frameworks, document processors, RAG orchestration tools) suitable for AWS deployment, documenting repositories, versions, licenses, and maturity indicators.

Assess each candidate's license compatibility (permissive vs. copyleft), security posture (CVE history, maintenance status), production readiness, AWS integration, scalability constraints, and alignment with enterprise security requirements for document handling.

Determine for each component whether to REUSE an existing open-source solution as-is, ADAPT an existing solution for AWS integration, or BUILD a custom wrapper, providing rationale based on evaluation results and project constraints.

Generate a detailed architecture blueprint specifying selected components, AWS services (S3, Lambda, RDS/DynamoDB, Cognito, API Gateway, etc.), deployment topology, data flow diagrams, integration points, security controls, and implementation sequence.

Validate that the blueprint satisfies all original requirements (PDF upload, OCR, secure storage, semantic search, RAG QA, authentication, APIs), identifies potential gaps, confirms license and security compliance, and highlights assumptions requiring stakeholder approval.
